name: Run-Pick
label: Run-Pick: pick a verb from the input list, run it on the clipboard (5 actions)

p.WFCommentActionText: Run-Choice in four cards. The input is the verb list, one name per line; the payload is the clipboard. No Get-Shortcut: Run Shortcut is a legacy action whose target is a plain string key, so the chosen NAME goes straight into WFWorkflowName. Run-Steps already proves it, carrying a bare token string there with no WFWorkflow dict at all. What is given up against Run-Choice: the self-demo prologue, and an arbitrary payload, since this one always reads the clipboard. The separator is stated rather than left to the default: Run-Choice omits it and its own sample is newline-separated, so the default is almost certainly New Lines, but a wrong guess here degrades quietly into a one-row menu rather than failing.
